subject: Modelling probability of detection in occu when known occupation is 1 in all sites

messages.author: d17a3321d5f25fa4
messages.subject: Modelling probability of detection in occu when known occupation is 1 in all sites
parts:
Dear all,
    We want to model probability of detections (single season, one species) by using obsCovs. 
All sites are occupied and we want to lock the parameter of occupancy to 1 (I-m attaching the file) 

We tried giving knownOcc values to all sites:
<-occu(~1 ~1,data,knownOcc=c(1:38))
But we get...Error: Hessian is singular.  Try providing starting values or using fewer covariates.

Then, we tried again giving some starting values...
<-occu(~1 ~1,data,knownOcc=c(1:38),starts=c(0,4))
But again...Error: Hessian is singular.  Try providing starting values or using fewer covariates.

We know we can use a glm and a logistic regression, but we would like to solve it with occu. Do you think it would be possible?

Thanks in advance,

Best regards

Igor

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Modelling probability of detection in occu when known occupation is 1 in all sites
parts:
Hi Igor,

why do you want to fit a logistic regression with an occupancy model ?

When occupancy probability psi is equal to 1, then you're back EXACTLY to a logistic regression for detection probability. Apart from satisfying your own curiosity or urge to play, there is absolutely no reason for using function occu then. You can use glm() or gam(), and with the latter you can for instance model arbitrary wiggly covariate relationships with detection.

(Having said that, yes, it should be possible to fit the logistic regression with occu also ....)

Kind regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Modelling probability of detection in occu when known occupation is 1 in all sites
parts:
Hi Igor,

I'm not sure why you wouldn't use a logistic regression, and I'm not sure if this will get around the singular Hessian, but you could try putting an upper bound on logit(psi):

occu(~1 ~1, data, knownOcc=1:38, method="L-BFGS-B", upper=c(10, Inf))

Richard

I agree with you that logistic regression is the way to solve it.
My curiosity was trying to understand why "occu" can not solve, in my case, an analysis when occupancy (Psi) = 1 in all sites.
If I define knownOcc for "all but one" sites, then "occu" can do it, and it find a solution.

It is not relevant, and I'm just playing with my data.
Again, thank you very much for being here and answering our doubts so quickly.

best

Igor
